content.text:
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The change is almost a faithful mirror of the existing `CheckOwnerCityCapacity` / `OwnerCityAtCapacityException` / handler / escalation-YAML / wiring pattern — naming, the Javadoc style, the `DAILY_LIMIT` constant mirroring `CITY_CAPACITY`, the checked-exception-carrying-context shape, and the pipeline placement (another guard step alongside the city-capacity check, before `build`) are all idiomatic and land in the right units. One concrete structural issue:

**`CheckOwnerDailyLimit.service` declares an unused `@Val OwnerFieldsDto request` parameter.**
- `src/main/java/.../owner/CheckOwnerDailyLimit.java:21` — the method takes `@Val OwnerFieldsDto request` but never reads it; the check only needs `ownerRepository`. This directly contradicts the codebase convention stated in AGENTS.md ("Declare only what the step needs"). Contrast with `CheckOwnerCityCapacity`, which takes `request` precisely *because* it uses `request.getCity()`. Drop the parameter so the signature is just `service(OwnerRepository ownerRepository) throws OwnerDailyLimitReachedException`.

Things I deliberately checked and found *not* to be problems (no change needed):
- The inlined `ownerRepository.findAll().stream().filter(...).count()` is **not** duplication that warrants an `OwnerCity`-style helper. `OwnerCity` exists only because two consumers (`CheckOwnerCityCapacity` and `AssignOwnerCustomerCode`) must agree on "same city." The "owners created today by registrationDate" count has a single consumer — the only other `registrationDate` use (`AssignOwnerMembershipNumber`) is unrelated formatting — so extracting a primitive here would be premature. Inlining is the right call.
- No class is becoming a catch-all; each new class has one responsibility consistent with its neighbors.
